title: Screens
intro: Twenty-six screens. Every app screen opens with a state switcher at the top — default, empty, loading, error, offline — and the sidebar carries the dark/light switch, the account and workspace menu, and the incoming-call notification.
reference_desc: Opened from any row in the calls list: the recording with its waveform, the transcript beside the whisper channel, and what the assistant did — summary, detected intent, tools invoked and the one that failed. Sets the vocabulary for everything else.

home.title: Home
home.desc: Needs your attention first, recent calls second, a deliberately minor dial card.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.desc: Things waiting on a human decision at the top, with the buttons that fix them; a thirty-day record of what was already dealt with below.

conversations.title: Channels
conversations.desc: Written conversations only — WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS and web chat — grouped by day. Calls have their own list; this screen is what someone typed.

calls.title: Calls list
calls.desc: Every call in a table, with full-text search across all transcripts.

call_detail.title: Call detail
call_detail.desc: One finished call opened from the list: the transcript beside what the assistant did about it.

live.title: Live calls
live.desc: Reached from the badge at the foot of the sidebar whenever something is on the line: every concurrent call on the left, the selected one's live transcript, whisper, take over and hand off on the right.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.desc: Week grid of the business diary, with everything the agent booked marked as such.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.desc: Customers and partners, and exactly which fields the assistant is allowed to use.

assistants.title: Assistants
assistants.desc: Every assistant with its type, number and last activity — plus a dark/light switch.

campaigns.title: Outbound campaigns
campaigns.desc: Calling a list instead of answering it. The running campaign sits on top with a live split of booked, reached, no answer and skipped; the four-step create flow settles who is called, what is said, and inside which hours.

consent.title: Consent log
consent.desc: Reached from Outbound campaigns. Every attempt with the reason it was allowed, a signed chain that cannot be edited after the fact, and the do-not-call list anyone lands on the second they say stop.

catalogue.title: Catalogue
catalogue.desc: What the business sells and what it records about the people who buy it — services with their length, price and whether the assistant may book them; contact fields each carrying its own permission; and a tab that shows the sentences the assistant can say from it.

editor.title: Edit assistant
editor.desc: Opened from a row in Assistants. Capability rows instead of one long form: enabled rows carry their current value, dormant ones a dashed border and a plus.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.desc: The shared source library and the structured opening hours. Reached from an assistant’s Answer questions panel, not from the sidebar.

rules.title: Routing rules
rules.desc: One ordered list read from the top — the first rule a call matches decides who answers, and a tester replays the list against any number to show which rule wins and which are never reached.

numbers.title: Numbers and phones
numbers.desc: Two tabs: the numbers the installation answers, and the desk phones, handsets and apps that ring as extensions on the line.

apps.title: Apps
apps.desc: Everything installable: channel apps for phone, WhatsApp and Telegram, plus tools the agent can use.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.desc: MCP tool servers the agent calls during a call: who runs each one, which of its tools may run, and what broke. The other direction — Tel-Agent as a server — stays in Settings.

usage.title: Usage
usage.desc: What the month cost, split by what actually charges money, against a budget that warns but never cuts the line.

settings.title: Settings
settings.desc: Nine tabs, defaults filled in, advanced kept out of the way. Reached from the account menu at the foot of the sidebar.

health.title: System health
health.desc: What is running and what is not: services, disk, model latency, and the checks that failed with the command that fixes each one.

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.desc: What is backed up, when it last ran, and a restore that says out loud what it will overwrite.

update.title: Update
update.desc: The version you run, what changed, and an update that can be rolled back.

install.title: Install and setup
install.desc: One flow from unpacking to the first call: language, install type, machine check, database and ports, then the phone line, the line of work that seeds the catalogue, the greeting, and ringing your own number.

workspace.title: New workspace
workspace.desc: A second business or location kept apart: name it, start empty or copy the current setup, decide who gets in.

login.title: Sign in
login.desc: Local accounts on your own server. No cloud login.

forgot.title: Reset password
forgot.desc: Ask for a code, or the command when there is no mail server.

code.title: Verification code
code.desc: Six digits, expiry and resend. The same screen serves two-factor sign-in.

new_password.title: New password
new_password.desc: Strength measured in the browser, and what changing it signs out.

key.title: Sign in with a key
key.desc: A challenge signed on your own machine. No password, no key upload.
